claim: The mammalian centrosome is a microtubule organizing center (MTOC) that plays a crucial role in mitotic spindle organization and cell polarity regulation.
source: The mammalian centrosome is a microtubule organizing center (MTOC) that plays a crucial role in various biological processes, such as mitotic spindle organization and cell polarity regulation (Oakley et al., 1990; Bystrevskaya et al., 1988; Bornens, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Oakley et al., 1990; Bystrevskaya et al., 1988; Bornens, 2012).

claim: A centrosome consists of a pair of rod-shaped centrioles (a mother centriole and a daughter centriole) and the pericentriolar material (PCM).
source: A centrosome consists of a pair of rod-shaped centrioles, i.e. a mother centriole and a daughter centriole, and the pericentriolar material (PCM).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about centrosome structure.

claim: γ-tubulin is considered as the major microtubule (MT)-nucleating factor of the PCM by forming the γ-tubulin ring complex (γTuRC) as the nucleation template.
source: γ‐tubulin is considered as the major microtubule (MT)‐nucleating factor of the PCM by forming the γ-tubulin ring complex (γTuRC) as the nucleation template (Moritz et al., 1995; Zheng et al., 1995; Pereira and Schiebel, 1997; Wiese and Zheng, 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations (Moritz et al., 1995; Zheng et al., 1995; Pereira and Schiebel, 1997; Wiese and Zheng, 1999).

claim: The size of the PCM indicated by the signal of γ-tubulin changes with the cell cycle, from a tightly packed PCM in the interphase to a large aggregate during mitosis.
source: The size of the PCM indicated by the signal of γ‐tubulin changes with the cell cycle, from a tightly packed PCM in the interphase to a large aggregate during mitosis, with the mother and daughter centrioles as the core (Khodjakov and Rieder, 1999; Robbins et al., 1968; Sonnen et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations (Khodjakov and Rieder, 1999; Robbins et al., 1968; Sonnen et al., 2012).

claim: The mother centriole is structurally differentiated from the daughter centriole by the presence of two appendage structures close to its distal end, namely distal appendages (DAPs) and subdistal appendages (sDAPs).
source: The mother centriole is structurally differentiated from the daughter centriole by the presence of two appendage structures close to its distal end, namely distal appendages (DAPs) and subdistal appendages (sDAPs).
evidence: This is established knowledge about centriole structure.

claim: DAPs are essential for centriole-membrane docking and primary cilia formation.
source: DAPs are essential for centriole-membrane docking and primary cilia formation (Tanos et al., 2013; Ye et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2012; Ishikawa et al., 2005; Joo et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations (Tanos et al., 2013; Ye et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2012; Ishikawa et al., 2005; Joo et al., 2013).

claim: A number of distal appendage (DAP) proteins have been identified, including C2CD3, CEP83, CEP89, SCLT1, FBF1 and CEP164.
source: We and others have identified a number of distal appendage (DAP) proteins, including C2CD3, CEP83, CEP89, SCLT1, FBF1 and CEP164 (Tanos et al., 2013; Ye et al., 2014; Graser et al., 2007; Wei et al., 2013; Sillibourne et al., 2013; Joo et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations (Tanos et al., 2013; Ye et al., 2014; Graser et al., 2007; Wei et al., 2013; Sillibourne et al., 2013; Joo et al., 2013).

claim: Super-resolution microscopy has been used to map the molecular architecture of mammalian DAPs toward the distal end of the mother centriole.
source: We have also used super-resolution microscopy to map the molecular architecture of mammalian DAPs toward the distal end of the mother centriole (Yang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous work (Yang et al., 2018).

claim: Super-resolved images showed that DAPs are composed of DAP blades of nine-fold symmetry and the novel structure of the DAP matrix between adjacent blades.
source: Super-resolved images showed that DAPs are composed of DAP blades of nine-fold symmetry, as observed in electron microscopy (EM), and the novel structure of the DAP matrix between adjacent blades.
evidence: The claim is based on super-resolution imaging data and comparison with EM observations.

claim: CEP89 occupies two longitudinal layers, one close to the DAP region and the other close to the putative subdistal appendage (sDAP) region.
source: We also found that CEP89 occupies two longitudinal layers, one close to the DAP region and the other close to the putative subdistal appendage (sDAP) region, proximally adjacent to the DAP region shown in a number of EM images of the mother centrioles.
evidence: The claim is based on super-resolution imaging observations and EM images.

claim: Some EM images showed variations in the number of sDAPs, such as 2 to 12 sDAP stems in human endotheliocytes.
source: Some EM images showed variations in the number of sDAPs, such as 2 to 12 sDAP stems in human endotheliocytes (Bystrevskaya et al., 1992; Bystrevskaya et al., 1988), illustrating the dynamic nature of sDAPs.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to EM studies (Bystrevskaya et al., 1992; Bystrevskaya et al., 1988).

claim: In contrast to an exact number of nine DAPs per centriole, the number of sDAPs may be different in different centrioles.
source: That is, in contrast to an exact number of nine DAPs per centriole, the number of sDAPs may be different in different centrioles (Uzbekov and Alieva, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation (Uzbekov and Alieva, 2018).

claim: Even when sDAPs do form a complete ring of nine-fold symmetry, their morphology is different from that of DAPs.
source: Even when sDAPs do form a complete ring of nine-fold symmetry, their morphology is different from that of DAPs (Paintrand et al., 1992; Uzbekov and Alieva, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations (Paintrand et al., 1992; Uzbekov and Alieva, 2018).

claim: Each sDAP stem is composed of one pair of electron-dense signals on the sides, where one of these signals is associated with the A-tubule of a MT triplet of the mother centriole and the other is associated with the C-tubule of an adjacent MT triplet.
source: Each sDAP stem is composed of one pair of electron-dense signals on the sides, where one of these signals is associated with the A-tubule of a MT triplet of the mother centriole and the other is associated with the C-tubule of an adjacent MT triplet (Bystrevskaya et al., 1988; Paintrand et al., 1992).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to EM studies (Bystrevskaya et al., 1988; Paintrand et al., 1992).

claim: The longitudinal positions of mammalian sDAPs may vary along the mother centriole.
source: The longitudinal positions of mammalian sDAPs may also vary along the mother centriole.
evidence: This is inferred from the variability observed in EM studies.

claim: For centrioles of motile cilia, the structure at the longitudinal position proximal to the DAPs is the basal foot, a 'badminton-shaped' structure that is largely different from the sDAPs in the mother centriole.
source: For centrioles of motile cilia, the structure at the longitudinal position proximal to the DAPs is the basal foot, a 'badminton-shaped' structure that is largely different from the sDAPs in the mother centriole (Anderson, 1972; Bornens, 2012; Bystrevskaya et al., 1988).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations (Anderson, 1972; Bornens, 2012; Bystrevskaya et al., 1988).

claim: The basal foot is oriented to align with the beating direction of motile cilia, suggesting its role in mechanical coupling or anchoring.
source: The basal foot is oriented to align with the beating direction of motile cilia, suggesting its role in mechanical coupling or anchoring (Gibbons, 1961; Clare et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations (Gibbons, 1961; Clare et al., 2014) and involves speculation about function.

claim: A series of sDAP proteins have been identified, including ODF2, CEP128, centriolin, CCDC68, CCDC120, ninein and CEP170.
source: We and others have identified a series of sDAP proteins, including ODF2, CEP128, centriolin, CCDC68, CCDC120, ninein and CEP170 (Mazo et al., 2016; Huang et al., 2017; Guarguaglini et al., 2005; Nakagawa et al., 2001; Ou et al., 2002; Mogensen et al., 2000; Schrøder et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations (Mazo et al., 2016; Huang et al., 2017; Guarguaglini et al., 2005; Nakagawa et al., 2001; Ou et al., 2002; Mogensen et al., 2000; Schrøder et al., 2012).

claim: DAPs are responsible for ciliogenesis and ciliary vesicle docking.
source: DAPs are responsible for ciliogenesis and ciliary vesicle docking (Tanos et al., 2013; Schmidt et al., 2012; Joo et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations (Tanos et al., 2013; Schmidt et al., 2012; Joo et al., 2013).

claim: sDAPs are mostly considered to serve roles in MT anchoring.
source: sDAPs are mostly considered to serve roles in MT anchoring (Vorobjev and Chentsov, 1982; Bystrevskaya et al., 1988; Bornens, 2002; Delgehyr et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations (Vorobjev and Chentsov, 1982; Bystrevskaya et al., 1988; Bornens, 2002; Delgehyr et al., 2005).

claim: EM images show that MTs terminate at the tips of sDAPs.
source: EM images show that MTs terminate at the tips of sDAPs, but one can also see many other MTs around the centrioles (Vorobjev and Chentsov, 1982; Mogensen et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to EM studies (Vorobjev and Chentsov, 1982; Mogensen et al., 2000).

claim: Centriole MT aster reformation after MT depolymerization is delayed in ninein or CEP170 knockout or knockdown cells.
source: Centriole MT aster reformation after MT depolymerization is delayed in ninein or CEP170 knockout or knockdown cells (Delgehyr et al., 2005; Guarguaglini et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations (Delgehyr et al., 2005; Guarguaglini et al., 2005).

claim: Both ninein and CEP170 have two localization populations, one at the centriole proximal end, and the other in the region close to sDAPs.
source: However, both ninein and CEP170 have two localization populations, one at the centriole proximal end, and the other in the region close to sDAPs (Sonnen et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation (Sonnen et al., 2012).

claim: Depletion of sDAPs together with the loss of the centriole proximal end protein CNAP1 results in the detachment of cilia and Golgi, affecting the positioning of primary cilia.
source: We have previously shown that, despite being dispensable for ciliogenesis, depletion of sDAPs together with the loss of the centriole proximal end protein CNAP1 results in the detachment of cilia and Golgi, affecting the positioning of primary cilia (Mazo et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous work (Mazo et al., 2016).

claim: CEP128 is implicated in RAB11 vesicle trafficking at the primary cilia, and CEP128 depletion results in a defect in TGF-β/bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling and abnormal organ development in zebrafish.
source: Another study on sDAP protein CEP128 found that CEP128 is implicated in RAB11 vesicle trafficking at the primary cilia, in which CEP128 depletion results in a defect in TGF-β/bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling and abnormal organ development in zebrafish (Mönnich et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation (Mönnich et al., 2018).

claim: A genetic knockout of the most upstream sDAP protein ODF2 in RPE-1 cells was shown to abolish the recruitment of other sDAP components.
source: In RPE-1 cells, a genetic knockout of the most upstream sDAP protein ODF2 was shown to abolish the recruitment of other sDAP components (Mazo et al., 2016), but neither the DAP assembly (Tanos et al., 2013) nor the ability of the mutant centrioles to grow cilia (Mazo et al., 2016) was grossly impacted.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations (Mazo et al., 2016; Tanos et al., 2013).

claim: Reduction of an upstream DAP protein, CEP83 in CEP83 mutated fibroblasts, did not affect the localization of ODF2.
source: Similarly, reduction of an upstream DAP protein, CEP83 in CEP83 mutated fibroblasts, did not affect the localization of ODF2 (Failler et al., 2014), suggesting that DAPs and sDAPs are two independent elements.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation (Failler et al., 2014).

claim: A null ODF2 knockout in the mouse F9 cell line abolished both the distal and subdistal appendages.
source: However, separate studies showed that a null ODF2 knockout in the mouse F9 cell line abolished both the distal and subdistal appendages (Ishikawa et al., 2005), and that partial truncation of ODF2 could abolish sDAPs without affecting DAPs (Tateishi et al., 2013), revealing a more complicated relationship between the two structures.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations (Ishikawa et al., 2005; Tateishi et al., 2013).

claim: Partial truncation of ODF2 could abolish sDAPs without affecting DAPs.
source: However, separate studies showed that a null ODF2 knockout in the mouse F9 cell line abolished both the distal and subdistal appendages (Ishikawa et al., 2005), and that partial truncation of ODF2 could abolish sDAPs without affecting DAPs (Tateishi et al., 2013), revealing a more complicated relationship between the two structures.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation (Tateishi et al., 2013).

claim: The study systematically characterized the super-resolved molecular architecture of sDAPs using direct stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (dSTORM).
source: In this study, we systematically characterized the super-resolved molecular architecture of sDAPs using direct stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (dSTORM).
evidence: This is a statement of the study's methodology.

claim: The study mapped the spatial organization of multiple sDAP-related proteins and generated a three-dimensional model.
source: We mapped the spatial organization of multiple sDAP-related proteins and generated a three-dimensional model.
evidence: This is a statement of the study's findings.

claim: The study found structural coupling between DAP and sDAP proteins.
source: Intriguingly, we found structural coupling between DAP and sDAP proteins.
evidence: This is a key finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: The study directly observed the role of sDAPs on MT anchoring.
source: We have also directly observed the role of sDAPs on MT anchoring and further illustrated the selective involvement of γ‐tubulins on MT templating.
evidence: This is a key finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: The study illustrated the selective involvement of γ-tubulins on MT templating.
source: We have also directly observed the role of sDAPs on MT anchoring and further illustrated the selective involvement of γ‐tubulins on MT templating.
evidence: This is a key finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: CEP170 exhibits a wider range of radial distributions under serum-fed (cell proliferating) conditions than under serum-starved (cell resting) conditions.
source: Statistically, CEP170 exhibits a wider range of radial distributions under serum-fed (cell proliferating) conditions than under serum-starved (cell resting) conditions (Figure 1b and c).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of imaging data shown in Figure 1b and c.

claim: Approximately 50% of ring occupancy is missing for CEP128 under serum-fed conditions, whereas approximately 25% is missing under serum-starved conditions.
source: Circular expansion of signals along the polar coordinate of the ring illustrates that ~50% of ring occupancy is missing under serum-fed conditions, whereas ~25% is missing under serum-starved conditions (Figure 1e and f).
evidence: The claim is supported by image analysis shown in Figure 1e and f.

claim: 24-hr serum starvation, which promotes ciliogenesis in around 60% of RPE-1 cells, has an effect on the completeness of ring occupancy of ciliogenesis-independent sDAP proteins.
source: It is interesting to note that 24-hr serum starvation, which promotes ciliogenesis in around 60% of RPE-1 cells (Lo et al., 2019), does have an effect on the completeness of ring occupancy of ciliogenesis-independent sDAP proteins.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations and cites a reference for the ciliogenesis rate (Lo et al., 2019).

claim: sDAPs may not always possess a nine-punctum pattern like that of DAPs in RPE-1 cells.
source: In addition, sDAPs may not always possess a nine-punctum pattern like that of DAPs in RPE-1 cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the imaging data showing variable occupancy patterns.

claim: ODF2 forms the smallest ring with a diameter similar to that of the centriole MT wall (~200 nm), suggesting its close proximity to the centriole.
source: Among them, ODF2 forms the smallest ring with a diameter similar to that of the centriole MT wall (~200 nm), suggesting its close proximity to the centriole.
evidence: The claim is based on diameter measurements from imaging data and involves inference about proximity.

claim: Ninein and CEP170 occupy a much wider space, with a diameter of around 600 nm, larger than the diameter of outer DAP proteins such as FBF1 and SCLT1.
source: By contrast, ninein and CEP170 occupy a much wider space, with a diameter of around 600 nm, larger than the diameter of outer DAP proteins such as FBF1 and SCLT1.
evidence: The claim is based on diameter measurements from imaging data.

claim: dSTORM images show a range of 250–600 nm in diameter for various sDAP proteins.
source: In line with previous SIM studies, our dSTORM images also show a range of 250–600 nm in diameter for various sDAP proteins.
evidence: The claim is based on measurements from dSTORM imaging data.

claim: The smaller the size of the protein distribution, the more upstream it is in the hierarchy of sDAP assembly.
source: When correlating the occupancies of sDAP proteins from ODF2 to CEP170 to the reported assembly hierarchy of sDAPs as illustrated in Figure 1h (Mazo et al., 2016; Huang et al., 2017), we found that the smaller the size of the protein distribution, the more upstream it is in the hierarchy.
evidence: The claim is based on correlation of imaging data with previously reported assembly hierarchy (Mazo et al., 2016; Huang et al., 2017).

claim: The overhang-like structure observed for ninein and CEP170 most probably comes from the proximal end localization of these proteins on the daughter centriole, and not from an overhang structure of the sDAPs.
source: When looking at these images together with conventional epifluorescent microscopy imaging (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), one can see that the extra signal most probably comes from the proximal end localization of CEP170 on the daughter centriole, and not from an overhang structure of the sDAPs.
evidence: The claim is based on 3D expansion microscopy and conventional microscopy imaging shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: TEM images reveal that sDAP stems can be mostly observed in the same section with a nine-fold arrangement.
source: The TEM images reveal that sDAP stems can be mostly observed in the same section with a nine-fold arrangement.
evidence: The claim is based on TEM imaging data shown in Figure 1i.

claim: The sDAP stems are mostly wider than those of DAPs.
source: It is also interesting to note that the sDAP stems are mostly wider than those of DAPs, similar to the observations recorded in previous work by the Bornens group (Paintrand et al., 1992).
evidence: The claim is based on TEM observations and cites a previous study (Paintrand et al., 1992).

claim: The stems of sDAPs are more flexible in shape and distribution than those of DAPs.
source: From the EM image, it seems that the stems of sDAPs are more flexible in shape and distribution than those of DAPs, potentially explaining the finding that nine-fold distribution is less obvious for the localization of sDAP proteins.
evidence: The claim is inferred from EM observations.

claim: CEP128 forms a compact layer at about 160 nm proximal to the SCLT1 layer of the DAPs.
source: As shown in Figure 2a and b, CEP128 forms a compact layer at about 160 nm proximal to the SCLT1 layer of the DAPs.
evidence: The claim is based on dual color dSTORM imaging data shown in Figure 2a and b.

claim: ODF2 covers a broader longitudinal region with two populations separating in two layers, which respectively localize at ~100 nm and ~200 nm proximal to the DAP protein SCLT1.
source: ODF2 covers a broader longitudinal region with two populations separating in two layers, which respectively localize at ~100 nm and ~200 nm proximal to the DAP protein SCLT1.
evidence: The claim is based on dual color dSTORM imaging data shown in Figure 2a and b.

claim: Centriolin covers a longitudinal range that seemingly possesses a single layer.
source: Centriolin also covers a longitudinal range that seemingly possesses a single layer, although we cannot rule out the possibility of two very close layers.
evidence: The claim is based on imaging data with some uncertainty acknowledged.

claim: Ninein and CEP170 localize both to the sDAP region and to the centriole proximal end marked by CNAP1, with the two layers separated by ~350 nm.
source: Ninein and CEP170 localize both to the sDAP region and to the centriole proximal end marked by CNAP1. The two layers are separated by ~350 nm.
evidence: The claim is based on dual color dSTORM imaging data.

claim: CEP128 is sandwiched between the two ODF2 layers, with centriolin localized above them.
source: CEP128 is sandwiched between the two ODF2 layers, with centriolin localized above them.
evidence: The claim is based on alignment of imaging data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Ninein and CEP170 localize radially outward from centriolin.
source: Ninein and CEP170 localize radially outward from centriolin.
evidence: The claim is based on imaging data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The composite image of sDAP proteins shows a left-right symmetric structure and each unit is triangular in shape.
source: The composite image of these sDAP proteins shows a left-right symmetric structure and each unit is triangular in shape.
evidence: The claim is based on composite imaging data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: ODF2 is located at the centriole wall and its two layers occupy the two ends of the sDAP root.
source: Assuming that CEP170 is localized at the tip of sDAP, as observed in the previous immune-EM study (Guarguaglini et al., 2005), ODF2 is located at the centriole wall and its two layers occupy the two ends of the sDAP root, that is the portion of an sDAP stem connecting to the centriole wall.
evidence: The claim is based on imaging data and inference from a previous study (Guarguaglini et al., 2005).

claim: CEP128 is right at the border between the centriole MT and the sDAP stem.
source: CEP128 is right at the border between the centriole MT and the sDAP stem.
evidence: The claim is based on the localization model derived from imaging data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Centriolin is located at the middle portion of an sDAP stem.
source: Centriolin is located at the middle portion of an sDAP stem, whereas ninein is close to the tips of sDAPs.
evidence: The claim is based on the localization model derived from imaging data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Ninein is close to the tips of sDAPs.
source: Centriolin is located at the middle portion of an sDAP stem, whereas ninein is close to the tips of sDAPs.
evidence: The claim is based on the localization model derived from imaging data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Both the sDAP protein ODF2 and the DAP protein CEP89 are two layered structures.
source: Note that both the sDAP protein ODF2 and the DAP protein CEP89 are two layered structures (Figure 3d,e).
evidence: The claim is based on imaging data shown in Figure 3d and e.

claim: The proximal layer of ODF2 is at the lowest position among the sDAP proteins studied.
source: The proximal layer of ODF2 is at the lowest position among the sDAP proteins studied; while the distal layer of ODF2 lies in close proximity to the core DAP protein CEP83 (i.e. ~60 nm proximal to SCLT1 as we previously reported; Yang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is based on imaging data and cites a previous study (Yang et al., 2018).

claim: The distal layer of ODF2 lies in close proximity to the core DAP protein CEP83 (~60 nm proximal to SCLT1).
source: The proximal layer of ODF2 is at the lowest position among the sDAP proteins studied; while the distal layer of ODF2 lies in close proximity to the core DAP protein CEP83 (i.e. ~60 nm proximal to SCLT1 as we previously reported; Yang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is based on imaging data and cites a previous study (Yang et al., 2018).

claim: The distal layer CEP89 lies at the distal end of DAPs.
source: The distal layer CEP89 lies at the distal end of DAPs; while its proximal layer is proximal to CEP83 and lies in the sDAP region.
evidence: The claim is based on imaging data shown in Figure 3d and e.

claim: The proximal layer of CEP89 is proximal to CEP83 and lies in the sDAP region.
source: The distal layer CEP89 lies at the distal end of DAPs; while its proximal layer is proximal to CEP83 and lies in the sDAP region.
evidence: The claim is based on imaging data shown in Figure 3d and e.

claim: The dual localization of ODF2 and CEP89 suggests a potential structural relationship between sDAPs and DAPs.
source: These observations suggest a potential structural relationship between sDAPs and DAPs.
evidence: This is inferred from the dual localization patterns observed in the imaging data.

claim: In DAP or sDAP knockout cells, single-layered ODF2 was observed.
source: Surprisingly, in DAP or sDAP knockout cells, single-layered ODF2 was observed (Figure 4b and e).
evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging of knockout cells shown in Figure 4b and e.

claim: The proximal layer of ODF2 was absent upon CEP128 depletion.
source: In particular, the proximal layer of ODF2 was absent upon CEP128 depletion, where SCLT1 was used as a reference of the longitudinal position.
evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging of CEP128 knockout cells shown in Figure 4b.

claim: In wild-type cells, ODF2-C distribution is wider than ODF2-N distribution in the radial direction.
source: dSTORM imaging of ODF2-C revealed that in wild-type cells, ODF2-C distribution is wider than ODF2-N distribution in the radial direction (Figure 4b, c and d).
evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging comparing two different ODF2 antibodies shown in Figure 4b, c and d.

claim: The distal edge of ODF2-C is closer to SCLT1 than that of ODF2-N, reaching further toward the centriole distal end.
source: In addition, the distal edge of ODF2-C is closer to SCLT1 than that of ODF2-N, reaching further toward the centriole distal end.
evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging comparing two different ODF2 antibodies shown in Figure 4b, c and d.

claim: When CEP128 is depleted, distributions of both ODF2-N and ODF2-C become thinner.
source: Interestingly, when CEP128 is depleted, distributions of both ODF2-N and ODF2-C become thinner.
evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging of CEP128 knockout cells shown in Figure 4c and d.

claim: The gap between ODF2-N/C and SCLT1 of CEP128–/– cells is larger than that of the wild-type cells.
source: The gap between ODF2-N/C and SCLT1 of CEP128–/– cells is larger than that of the wild-type cells, illustrating both narrowing and shifting of ODF2 occupancy upon sDAP CEP128 depletion.
evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging of CEP128 knockout cells shown in Figure 4c and d.

claim: CEP128, as the binding partner of ODF2, regulates the organization of ODF2.
source: These observations imply that CEP128, as the binding partner of ODF2 (Kashihara et al., 2019), regulates the organization of ODF2.
evidence: The claim is inferred from imaging data and cites a previous study (Kashihara et al., 2019).

claim: In CEP83-depleted centrioles, one layer of ODF2 was absent.
source: Similarly, in CEP83-depleted centrioles, one layer of ODF2 was absent (Figure 4e).
evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging of CEP83 knockout cells shown in Figure 4e.

claim: ODF2 is associated with both DAPs and sDAPs as a downstream protein of CEP83 and CEP128, respectively.
source: This observation implies that ODF2 is associated with both DAPs and sDAPs as a downstream protein of CEP83 and CEP128, respectively.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the knockout experiments showing loss of ODF2 layers upon depletion of CEP83 or CEP128.

claim: The finding of one layer of ODF2 as a downstream protein of CEP128 explains previous genetic studies showing reduced ODF2 levels due to CEP128 depletion.
source: Note that our finding here of one layer of ODF2 as a downstream protein of CEP128 explains our previous genetic studies showing reduced ODF2 levels due to CEP128 depletion (Mazo et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim connects current findings with previous genetic studies (Mazo et al., 2016).

claim: The proximal layer of CEP89 was absent when sDAP was depleted.
source: Intriguingly, the proximal layer of CEP89 was absent when sDAP was depleted (Figure 4f and g).
evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging of CEP128 knockout cells shown in Figure 4f and g.

claim: CEP89 signal was reduced when DAP was depleted as compared to that in the wild type cells.
source: While DAP was depleted, CEP89 signal was reduced as compared to that in the wild type cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Similar to ODF2, CEP89 has dual roles associated with both DAPs and sDAPs.
source: That is, similar to ODF2, CEP89 has dual roles associated with both DAPs and sDAPs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the knockout experiments showing effects on CEP89 localization upon depletion of either DAPs or sDAPs.

claim: In DAP-depleted CEP83–/–cells, ninein at the sDAPs covers a longitudinal region larger than that in wild-type cells.
source: Surprisingly, super-resolution images show that in DAP-depleted CEP83–/–cells, ninein at the sDAPs covers a longitudinal region larger than that in wild-type cells (Figure 4g and h).
evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging of CEP83 knockout cells shown in Figure 4h and i.

claim: The broadened longitudinal region of ninein spans from the sDAP region to the region originally occupied by DAPs.
source: Using CP110 as a reference to indicate the distal boundary of the centriole, we find that the broadened longitudinal region of ninein spans from the sDAP region to the region originally occupied by DAPs.
evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging using CP110 as a reference marker shown in Figure 4h and i.

claim: When CEP83 is stably expressed in CEP83–/– cells (CEP83–/– Rescue), the sDAP distribution of ninein is restored.
source: In addition, when CEP83 is stably expressed in CEP83–/–cells (CEP83–/– Rescue), the sDAP distribution of ninein is restored (Figure 4h and i).
evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging of rescue cells shown in Figure 4h and i.

claim: In wild-type cells, sDAPs mostly maintained their longitudinal position close to and proximal to the DAPs, but their shapes varied in different centrioles or even in the same centriole.
source: In wild-type cells, sDAPs mostly maintained their longitudinal position close to and proximal to the DAPs, but their shapes varied in different centrioles or even in the same centriole (Figure 4j, left panel).
evidence: The claim is based on TEM observations shown in Figure 4j.

claim: The sDAP structure is much less stable when DAPs are missing.
source: That is, the sDAP structure is much less stable when DAPs are missing.
evidence: This is inferred from the TEM observations showing variable sDAP structures in CEP83 knockout cells.

claim: The loss of DAPs via CEP83 depletion affects the structural stability of sDAPs, providing further evidence that DAPs and sDAPs are structurally related to each other.
source: These large variations imply that the loss of DAPs via CEP83 depletion affects the structural stability of sDAPs, providing further evidence that DAPs and sDAPs are structurally related to each other (Figure 4k).
evidence: This is inferred from the TEM and super-resolution imaging observations of CEP83 knockout cells.

claim: The absence of ninein reduced microtubule (MT) regrowth after nocodazole-induced MT depolymerization.
source: Previous studies have shown that the absence of ninein reduced microtubule (MT) regrowth after nocodazole-induced MT depolymerization (Delgehyr et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Delgehyr et al., 2005).

claim: In widefield images, no observable difference is found in terms of centrioles serving as the center of MT networks between wild-type and CEP128–/– RPE-1 cells during the serum-starved G0 phase.
source: In widefield images, no observable difference is found in terms of centrioles serving as the center of MT networks (Figure 5a and b).
evidence: The claim is based on widefield imaging data shown in Figure 5a and b.

claim: By overlaying multiple lateral super-resolved α-tubulin images of wild-type and CEP128–/–cells, a void region of MTs in the sDAP region of CEP128–/– cells was found.
source: Excitingly, by overlaying multiple lateral super-resolved α-tubulin images of wild-type and CEP128–/–cells, we are able to find a void region of MTs in the sDAP region of CEP128–/– cells (Figure 5e, f and g).
evidence: The claim is based on super-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 5e, f and g.

claim: This is the first evidence from high-resolution imaging to show that loss of sDAPs results in loss of MT attachments.
source: While previous EM studies have revealed the proximity of MTs and sDAPs (Mogensen et al., 2000), this is the first evidence from high-resolution imaging to show that loss of sDAPs results in loss of MT attachments.
evidence: The claim is based on the super-resolution imaging data and cites a previous EM study (Mogensen et al., 2000).

claim: The study illustrates a direct role for sDAP in MT anchoring.
source: It illustrates a direct role for sDAP in MT anchoring.
evidence: This is concluded from the super-resolution imaging showing loss of MTs at sDAPs upon CEP128 depletion.

claim: Lateral-view images show another subset of MTs that terminate at the DAP region.
source: In addition to sDAP's role in anchoring MTs, our lateral-view images also show another subset of MTs that terminate at the DAP region (Figure 5e and f).
evidence: The claim is based on super-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 5e and f.

claim: DAP-associated MTs do not seem to be affected by sDAP depletion.
source: These DAP-associated MTs do not seem to be affected by sDAP depletion.
evidence: This is inferred from the imaging data comparing wild-type and CEP128 knockout cells.

claim: γ-tubulins are highly enriched close to the centriole.
source: As expected, γ-tubulins are highly enriched close to the centriole (Figure 6a).
evidence: The claim is based on super-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: Most γ-tubulins cover the longitudinal region of the mother centriole from the proximal end to the height of the sDAPs, leaving the region between the DAPs and sDAPs less populated.
source: Intriguingly, super-resolution imaging shows that most γ-tubulins cover the longitudinal region of the mother centriole from the proximal end to the height of the sDAPs (Figure 6a), leaving the region between the DAPs and sDAPs less populated.
evidence: The claim is based on super-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The diameter of the γ-tubulin occupied region is about 400 nm, larger than the diameter of the centriole.
source: The diameter of the γ-tubulin occupied region is about 400 nm, larger than the diameter of the centriole (Figure 6b).
evidence: The claim is based on diameter measurements from super-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: γ-tubulins in the G0 phase are mostly confined to a well-defined cylindrical position outside the mother centriole.
source: That is, γ-tubulins in the G0 phase are mostly confined to a well-defined cylindrical position outside the mother centriole.
evidence: This is inferred from the imaging data showing the spatial distribution of γ-tubulins.

claim: This confined cylindrical distribution of γ-tubulins provides a better-defined localization of the previously known tightly packed PCM in the interphase.
source: This confined cylindrical distribution of γ-tubulins provides a better-defined localization of the previously known tightly packed PCM in the interphase, which is very different from the broad distribution of PCM-bound γ-tubulins during mitosis.
evidence: This is inferred from the imaging data and comparison with known PCM behavior during the cell cycle.

claim: The distal α-tubulin enrichment close to the sDAP region is different from the relatively uniform longitudinal distribution of γ-tubulin.
source: When compared to the distribution of α-tubulin of wild-type centrioles shown in Figure 5f, the distal α-tubulin enrichment close to the sDAP region is different from the relatively uniform longitudinal distribution of γ-tubulin.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the distributions of α-tubulin and γ-tubulin in the imaging data.

claim: There are at least two populations of γ-tubulins: a major population that does not anchor α- and β-tubulins and localizes along the mother centriole, and another associated with MT anchoring at the sDAP region.
source: Therefore, it is likely that there are at least two populations of γ-tubulins, a major population that does not anchor α- and β-tubulins and localizes along the mother centriole, and the other associated with MT anchoring at the sDAP region.
evidence: This is inferred from the different distributions of α-tubulin and γ-tubulin observed in the imaging data.

claim: Averaging the signals of several centrioles shows statistically significant γ-tubulin signal reduction in the sDAP tip region of CEP128–/– cells.
source: Averaging the signals of several centrioles shows statistically significant signal reduction in the sDAP tip region of CEP128–/– cells (Figure 6d).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of imaging data shown in Figure 6d.

claim: sDAPs spatially regulate the distal boundary of γ-tubulins along the centriole.
source: That is, sDAPs spatially regulate the distal boundary of γ-tubulins along the centriole.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that γ-tubulin distribution changes upon sDAP depletion.

claim: The population of γ-tubulins that spreads distally in CEP128–/– cells may not anchor MTs, because decreased α-tubulin population was observed at the distal end of the mother centriole in the CEP128–/–cells.
source: Furthermore, this population of γ-tubulins may not anchor MTs, because we observed decreased α-tubulin population at the distal end of the mother centriole in the CEP128–/–cells. as summarized in a speculative model in Figure 5g.
evidence: This is inferred from the imaging data and involves speculation about function.

claim: A population of γ-tubulins at the sDAP tips is responsible for the nucleation of specific MTs from the sDAPs.
source: It is possible that a population of γ-tubulins at the sDAP tips is responsible for the nucleation of specific MTs from the sDAPs, although the specific functions of these MTs remain elusive.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the imaging data.

claim: The study mapped the molecular architecture of sDAPs together with DAPs using super-resolution microscopy to gain a more comprehensive structural understanding of the distal end of the mother centriole.
source: We have mapped the molecular architecture of sDAPs together with DAPs using super-resolution microscopy to gain a more comprehensive structural understanding of the distal end of the mother centriole.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the study's approach and findings.

claim: Unlike the more consistent nine-fold symmetric structures of DAP proteins, sDAP proteins are less organized, either with an incomplete occupancy of the ring or a spreading radial distribution.
source: Unlike the more consistent nine-fold symmetric structures of DAP proteins, sDAP proteins are less organized, either with an incomplete occupancy of the ring or a spreading radial distribution.
evidence: This is a summary of the imaging observations comparing DAP and sDAP protein distributions.

claim: For sDAPs possessing a more complete ring-shaped occupancy, ODF2, CEP128, and centriolin form better-defined nine puncta-like structures, whereas CCDC68, ninein, and CEP170 distribute more randomly around a ring.
source: For those sDAPs possessing a more complete ring-shaped occupancy, ODF2, CEP128, and centriolin form better-defined nine puncta-like structures, whereas CCDC68, ninein, and CEP170 distribute more randomly around a ring.
evidence: This is a summary of the imaging observations of different sDAP proteins.

claim: The genetic and localization relationships of ODF2 and CEP128 are consistent with the finding that these two proteins form a protein complex to work together as an sDAP component.
source: The genetic and localization relationships of ODF2 and CEP128 are consistent with the finding that these two proteins form a protein complex to work together as an sDAP component (Kashihara et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim connects the study's findings with a previous study (Kashihara et al., 2019).

claim: The measurement may differ depending on the epitope regions of the protein of interest, as observed using ODF2 antibodies that recognize each terminus of the protein.
source: Note that the measurement may differ depending on the epitope regions of the protein of interest, as observed using ODF2 antibodies that recognize each terminus of the protein (Figure 4d).
evidence: This is based on the observation of different localization patterns using different antibodies shown in Figure 4d.

claim: This difference in structural arrangement may be related to the different functions of the N and C termini of ODF2 suggested in previous studies.
source: This difference in structural arrangement may be related to the different functions of the N and C termini of ODF2 suggested in previous studies (Ishikawa et al., 2005; Kashihara et al., 2019), with the N terminus of ODF2 found to be the interacting domain for CEP128.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning connecting the study's observations with previous studies (Ishikawa et al., 2005; Kashihara et al., 2019).

claim: DAPs serve as a distal border of sDAPs.
source: That is, DAPs serve as a distal border of sDAPs.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that ninein distribution changes upon DAP depletion.

claim: The structural arrangement of sDAPs is dependent on the structural arrangement of DAPs.
source: The structural arrangement of sDAPs is dependent on the structural arrangement of DAPs.
evidence: This is inferred from the observations showing changes in sDAP structure upon DAP depletion.

claim: Removal of sDAPs does not influence ciliogenesis, which requires proper functions of DAPs.
source: Removal of sDAPs does not influence ciliogenesis, which requires proper functions of DAPs (Mazo et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Mazo et al., 2016).

claim: sDAP protein localizations are still observed upon depletion of DAPs.
source: sDAP protein localizations are still observed upon depletion of DAPs (Joo et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Joo et al., 2013).

claim: Using super-resolution microscopy, the study shows that DAPs and sDAPs are not entirely independent, with at least two proteins serving dual roles and with ninein positioning affected by the DAP structure.
source: On the other hand, using super-resolution microscopy, we show here that DAPs and sDAPs are not entirely independent, with at least two proteins serving dual roles and with ninein positioning affected by the DAP structure (Figure 4i).
evidence: This is a key conclusion of the study based on the experimental data.

claim: The study provides direct evidence that sDAP-specific CEP128 knockout depletes MT population close to the sDAPs, further confirming that sDAPs anchor a subset of MTs around the mother centriole.
source: We also provide direct evidence that sDAP-specific CEP128 knockout depletes MT population close to the sDAPs, further confirming that sDAPs anchor a subset of MTs around the mother centriole (Figure 6g).
evidence: This is a key finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: This result clarifies the previous conclusion of ninein's role in MT anchoring as an sDAP element.
source: This result clarifies the previous conclusion of ninein's role in MT anchoring as an sDAP element (Delgehyr et al., 2005; Mogensen et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim connects the study's findings with previous studies (Delgehyr et al., 2005; Mogensen et al., 2000).

claim: One speculation is that the sDAP-anchoring MTs are related to the mechanosensation of cells.
source: One speculation would be related to the mechanosensation of cells through this subset of sDAP-anchoring MTs.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about the potential function of sDAP-anchoring MTs.

claim: For a motile cilium, the component proximal to DAPs is a cone-shaped basal foot, whose orientation is aligned to its beating direction, serving as a mechanical coupling element at the ciliary base.
source: It is known that for a motile cilium, the component proximal to DAPs is a cone-shaped basal foot, whose orientation is aligned to its beating direction, serving as a mechanical coupling element at the ciliary base (Clare et al., 2014; Bornens, 2012; Gibbons, 1961).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations (Clare et al., 2014; Bornens, 2012; Gibbons, 1961).

claim: Because a primary cilium does not actively beat, it is speculated that mechanosensation is required in all orientations, thus the ring-shaped sDAPs are formed at the centriolar distal end to anchor mechanosensing MTs in all circumferential directions.
source: Because a primary cilium does not actively beat, it is speculated that mechanosensation is required in all orientations. Thus the ring-shaped sDAPs are formed at the centriolar distal end to anchor mechanosensing MTs in all circumferential directions.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about the potential function of sDAPs in primary cilia.

claim: Another possibility is that the subset of sDAP-anchoring MTs partially bridges a centriole and Golgi apparatus.
source: Another possibility is that this subset of MTs partially bridges a centriole and Golgi apparatus, because we have previously shown that even though Golgi remains adjacent to a centriole in single knockout of CEP128–/–, double knockouts of CEP128–/– and CNAP1–/– result in centriole-Golgi dissociation (Mazo et al., 2016).
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on previous findings (Mazo et al., 2016).

claim: In the G0 quiescent phase, there is one population of γ-tubulins involved in MT anchoring at sDAPs, and another population of γ-tubulins localized along the centriole that is not associated with the α-tubulin population.
source: From these results, we can speculate that, in the G0 quiescent phase, there is one population of γ-tubulins involved in MT anchoring at sDAPs, and another population of γ-tubulins localized along the centriole that is not associated with the α-tubulin population.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the imaging data.

claim: The major γ-tubulin population in G0 phase wraps around the mother centriole at a well-defined cylindrical confinement with sDAPs as their distal constraint.
source: The latter population comprises the majority of centrosomal γ-tubulins and wraps around the mother centriole at a well-defined cylindrical confinement with sDAPs as their distal constraint.
evidence: This is inferred from the imaging data showing γ-tubulin distribution.

claim: It is possible that these γ-tubulins are anchored at the compact PCM structure outside the mother centriole, with a diameter larger than the centriole wall, illustrating a clear shape of the confined PCM during interphase.
source: It is possible that these γ-tubulins are anchored at the compact PCM structure outside the mother centriole, with a diameter larger than the centriole wall, illustrating a clear shape of the confined PCM during interphase.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the imaging data.

claim: It is possible that the major γ-tubulin population in G0 phase serves as a reservoir of MT nucleating sites, which enables quick initiation of MT growth once the cells re-enter the cell cycle.
source: It is also possible that this major γ-tubulin population in G0 phase serves as a reservoir of MT nucleating sites, which enables quick initiation of MT growth once the cells re-enter the cell cycle.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about the potential function of the major γ-tubulin population.

claim: MT initiation and anchoring may be independent processes.
source: Besides, as suggested by a previous study showing that MT initiation and anchoring may be independent processes (Delgehyr et al., 2005), it is also likely that these γ-tubulins can first initiate MT nucleation around the centriole and later be associated with some MT-anchoring proteins, such as ninein, to anchor MT to sDAPs.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Delgehyr et al., 2005) and involves speculation.

claim: It is likely that these γ-tubulins can first initiate MT nucleation around the centriole and later be associated with some MT-anchoring proteins, such as ninein, to anchor MT to sDAPs.
source: Besides, as suggested by a previous study showing that MT initiation and anchoring may be independent processes (Delgehyr et al., 2005), it is also likely that these γ-tubulins can first initiate MT nucleation around the centriole and later be associated with some MT-anchoring proteins, such as ninein, to anchor MT to sDAPs.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on a previous study (Delgehyr et al., 2005).
